A technology company still earns a third of its profit from a legacy product it stopped actively developing years ago; the replacement product is stronger but lacks a few niche features that the most loyal legacy customers depend on. Maintenance costs and security exposure on the old platform grow every year, and the engineers who understand it are approaching retirement. Some large customers threaten to switch vendors entirely if forced to migrate.

Plan the end-of-life and migration program for the legacy product. Set the sunset timeline and support policy, decide which niche capabilities must be rebuilt versus retired, design migration incentives and tooling for each customer tier, and prepare the retention plan for the customers most likely to defect during the transition.

[ORIGINAL USER REQUEST]
A technology company still earns a third of its profit from a legacy product it stopped actively developing years ago; the replacement product is stronger but lacks a few niche features that the most loyal legacy customers depend on. Maintenance costs and security exposure on the old platform grow every year, and the engineers who understand it are approaching retirement. Some large customers threaten to switch vendors entirely if forced to migrate.

Plan the end-of-life and migration program for the legacy product. Set the sunset timeline and support policy, decide which niche capabilities must be rebuilt versus retired, design migration incentives and tooling for each customer tier, and prepare the retention plan for the customers most likely to defect during the transition.
[END ORIGINAL REQUEST]

[PREVIOUS AGENT OUTPUT]
To successfully sunset a legacy product while preserving customer loyalty and mitigating technical risk, you must transition from a "maintenance" mindset to a "migration partnership" model.

The following plan outlines a **24-month sunset strategy**, structured to de-risk the technical debt while incentivizing high-value customers to move.

---

### 1. The Sunset Timeline (24 Months)
The timeline assumes a gradual "sunsetting by degrees" to minimize disruption.

*   **Months 1–6 (Preparation):** Build the migration toolkit, finalize feature parity requirements, and launch the internal "knowledge transfer" program (pairing junior engineers with retiring experts).
*   **Months 7–12 (Early Adopter Phase):** Launch the migration incentive program. Begin "Sunset Warnings" on the legacy UI.
*   **Months 13–18 (General Migration):** Formal End-of-Sales (EOS) for legacy renewals. Shift legacy pricing to a premium, "extended support" model.
*   **Months 19–24 (The Home Stretch):** Final countdown to End-of-Life (EOL). Force-migration paths or third-party archiving services provided.

---

### 2. Feature Parity & Engineering Strategy
Do not rebuild the legacy product 1:1. Use a **"Core + Plugin"** architecture for the new product.

*   **Categorization:** 
    *   *Core Features:* Migrate to the new product’s native stack.
    *   *Niche/Legacy Features:* Build these as **API-driven micro-services or modular plugins** that plug into the new product. This avoids bloating the main codebase.
    *   *Retired Features:* Decommission features with <1% usage. Provide a CSV data-export tool to allow customers to keep historical data locally.
*   **Legacy Knowledge Retention:** Implement a "Consultant-in-Residence" program. Offer retiring engineers part-time, post-retirement contracts to serve as architectural advisors for the migration team.

---

### 3. Customer Tiering & Migration Incentives
Treat your customers based on their propensity to churn versus their total account value.

| Tier | Strategy | Incentive |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Strategic/Enterprise** | High-touch Concierge | Dedicated migration engineer, custom feature development, white-glove data mapping. |
| **Mid-Market** | Self-Service + Support | Migration credits (6 months free), automated data import tools, training webinars. |
| **Legacy/Small** | Automated Sunset | Standardized documentation, discounted transition pricing, "End of Life" deadline notification. |

---

### 4. Technical Migration Tooling
To reduce the friction of switching, you must build the "Bridge":

*   **The Data Mover:** A "one-click" import utility that maps legacy schemas to the new data model.
*   **The "Legacy-Compat" Proxy:** If the new platform allows, build a middleware layer that supports legacy API calls, allowing customers to keep some legacy integrations running while they migrate their UI workflows.
*   **Validation Suite:** A tool that runs post-migration to verify data integrity and alert the customer to any discrepancies.

---

### 5. Retention & Defection Mitigation
The threat of customers switching vendors is highest for "loyalists" who rely on niche features.

*   **The "Grandfathered Niche" Program:** For the most critical, high-risk enterprise accounts, offer a **"Hybrid Support Contract."** They move to the new product for 90% of their business, but you maintain the legacy instance for 12 months *only for them* at a significant price premium that covers the cost of maintaining the legacy team.
*   **The "Lock-In" Discount:** Offer multi-year contracts on the new product at the legacy price point to neutralize price-based churn.
*   **Voice of the Customer (VoC):** Conduct "Sunset Interviews." Find out exactly *why* they refuse to move. Often, it is not just the missing feature, but the risk of downtime. Address that fear with a **"Rollback Guarantee"**—if the migration fails to meet performance benchmarks within 30 days, you provide a rollback plan to their legacy instance.

---

### 6. Success Metrics (KPIs)
Monitor these metrics monthly to gauge the health of the transition:
1.  **Migration Velocity:** Number of customers moved per month.
2.  **Legacy Deprecation Rate:** Percentage of total legacy features effectively decommissioned.
3.  **Churn Risk Score:** A dashboard tracking the sentiment of high-value accounts identified during the Tiering phase.
4.  **Engineering Resource Allocation:** Monitoring the shift of hours from "Legacy Maintenance" to "New Product Development."

### Final Recommendation
Stop selling the legacy product to new customers immediately. Communicate to existing customers that the **Legacy platform is a liability, not an asset, to their own security.** By framing the migration as a security upgrade, you move the conversation from "feature loss" to "business continuity."
[END PREVIOUS OUTPUT]

### Critical Review of Previous Output

**Strengths:**
*   **Strategic Structure:** The 24-month timeline provides a realistic window for enterprise migrations.
*   **Actionable Engineering Approach:** The suggestion of an "API-driven micro-services" architecture for niche features is an industry-standard best practice for managing tech debt without bloating core platforms.
*   **Customer Segmentation:** The tiered strategy correctly prioritizes high-value, high-risk accounts.

**Weaknesses and Areas for Improvement:**
*   **Financial Reality Gap:** The prompt states the company earns **a third of its profit** from the legacy product. The current plan frames the legacy product as a "liability" (which is true for security) but fails to address the *profitability cliff* the company will face. A more rigorous financial strategy (e.g., transition pricing models that prevent immediate revenue loss) is missing.
*   **Legal and Contractual Risks:** The plan lacks mention of service-level agreements (SLAs). If large customers threaten to leave, they likely have contractual holdover clauses or data residency requirements that need to be addressed in the migration documentation.
*   **"Retiring Expert" Risk:** The "Consultant-in-Residence" program is a good idea, but it lacks a "bus factor" mitigation strategy. If the retiring experts leave before the 24 months are up, the migration team is paralyzed.
*   **Lack of Communication Strategy:** While the "Sunset Warning" is mentioned, there is no detailed communication roadmap. Managing the messaging to prevent a panic-driven churn (where customers leave early because they fear the product is already "dead") is critical.

1.  **Add a Financial Impact Analysis:** Include a bridge plan to ensure the new product’s margin offsets the loss of the legacy product's high-margin, low-maintenance revenue.
2.  **Formalize the "Retirement Risk" Mitigation:** Build in an immediate "Knowledge Capture" sprint (documenting code, API behaviors, and tribal knowledge) within the first 90 days, rather than relying solely on the experts' availability.
3.  **Include an "Early Warning System":** Add a proactive communication phase to help customers realize the migration is a benefit (e.g., performance, security compliance) before they see the sunset notice.

To successfully sunset a legacy product while preserving one-third of the company’s profit, the strategy must shift from a "maintenance" mindset to a "value-migration" model. The goal is to migrate high-margin revenue to the new platform while systematically de-risking the technical and human-capital debt.

### 1. The Financial Bridge & Profitability Strategy
Because the legacy product provides 33% of profits, a premature sunset is an existential threat.
*   **The "Profit Floor" Model:** Do not immediately discount the new product. Implement a **Legacy Premium Pricing (LPP)** model during the transition. As legacy maintenance costs (security patches, server upkeep) rise, pass these costs to holdouts via a "Legacy Surcharge." 
*   **Value-Linked Migration:** Offer "Loyalty Credit" transfers. Customers migrating to the new platform receive a credit based on their legacy tenure, but only if they sign a 3-year term on the new product. This locks in revenue and protects the company’s EBITDA during the transition period.
*   **Margin Balancing:** Use the LPP revenue to fund the "feature-rebuild" team. By year 2, the goal is for the cost savings from decommissioning legacy infrastructure to offset the margin lost from legacy holdouts.

### 2. Retirement Risk & Knowledge Capture (Months 0–6)
To mitigate the "bus factor" of retiring engineers, shift from informal consulting to **Structural Knowledge Capture.**
*   **The 90-Day Sprint:** Within the first 90 days, launch an intensive documentation and instrumentation sprint. Retiring experts are tasked exclusively with creating a "Legacy Knowledge Base," including architectural decision records (ADRs), edge-case documentation, and "black box" API behavior mapping.
*   **Shadow Engineering:** Pair every junior engineer assigned to the migration with one retiring expert. Require the junior to perform the actual coding for legacy patches under the expert's review for the first 6 months.
*   **Retirement Incentives:** Offer "stay bonuses" tied to the successful completion of the knowledge transfer milestones, rather than just the passage of time.

### 3. The 24-Month Sunset Timeline
*   **Phase 1 (Months 1–6: Preservation & Capture):** Knowledge capture sprint, internal API mapping, and initial "Early Warning" customer communications focusing on the benefits of the new platform (speed, security compliance).
*   **Phase 2 (Months 7–12: Feature Parity & Pilot):** Launch "Bridge Tools" (data migrators). Pilot the migration with mid-tier customers to refine the process.
*   **Phase 3 (Months 13–18: General Migration & LPP):** End of Sales (EOS) for new legacy contracts. Introduce the "Legacy Surcharge" for renewals.
*   **Phase 4 (Months 19–24: Forced Transition):** Sunset support for legacy environments. Customers remaining are migrated to a "Legacy Archive" instance with limited, self-service support.

### 4. Communication Strategy: "Security as a Service"
To prevent panic-driven churn, the messaging must change:
*   **The Narrative:** Stop calling it a "Sunset." Call it a **"Performance & Security Upgrade."**
*   **The Early Warning System:** Start by releasing high-value, performant features on the new platform that are impossible on the legacy one. Let customers "pull" themselves toward the new platform through feature envy rather than being "pushed" by the sunset.
*   **Transparency:** Provide a public roadmap showing exactly when legacy features will reach EOL, giving enterprise clients the lead time required for their internal IT procurement cycles.

### 5. Legal, Contractual, & Technical Compliance
*   **SLA Harmonization:** Review all enterprise contracts. Ensure the transition plan includes a "SLA Guarantee" that the migration will not result in a loss of service levels. If a niche feature is retired, offer a contractual "Custom Integration Service" (at a fee) to build a bespoke bridge for that specific client.
*   **Data Residency:** Many legacy customers stay due to data residency compliance. Ensure the new platform has parity in regional data centers/cloud availability zones before forcing migration.
*   **The "Rollback Guarantee":** To mitigate the fear of migration-related downtime, contractually promise a "Snapshot & Rollback" window. If the migration causes a major regression, the company will provide a temporary revert to the legacy instance at no cost to the customer.

### 6. Success Metrics
*   **Profit Neutrality:** Tracking if new product revenue growth offsets legacy profit loss monthly.
*   **Legacy Knowledge Index:** A measurement of how much of the legacy codebase is fully documented and understood by at least two non-retiring engineers.
*   **Migration Net Promoter Score (mNPS):** Tracking sentiment specifically among customers currently undergoing the migration process.
*   **Cost-per-Legacy-Seat:** Monitoring the rising cost of supporting legacy users to validate the "Legacy Surcharge" pricing.
